title: Python GPIO on Raspberry Pi
subtitle: RPi.GPIO, gpiozero, and controlling hardware with Python

content.text: Raspberry Pi GPIO uses 3.3V logic. Python's gpiozero library provides a high-level interface for buttons, LEDs, motors, and sensors.

content.code:
from gpiozero import LED, Button
from signal import pause

led = LED(17)      # GPIO17 = pin 11
btn = Button(27)   # GPIO27 = pin 13

btn.when_pressed  = led.on
btn.when_released = led.off

pause()  # wait forever for events

from gpiozero import PWMLED
from time import sleep

led = PWMLED(17)

# Fade in and out
while True:
    for brightness in range(0, 100, 5):
        led.value = brightness / 100
        sleep(0.05)
    for brightness in range(100, 0, -5):
        led.value = brightness / 100
        sleep(0.05)

content.text: Always use GPIO.cleanup() (or let gpiozero do it automatically) when your script exits, to reset pin states.

questions.question: What voltage level do Raspberry Pi GPIO pins use?
questions.explanation: Raspberry Pi GPIO pins are 3.3V. Never connect 5V signals directly — it will damage the Pi.

faq.q: Can I use an Arduino sensor library on Raspberry Pi?
faq.a: No. Arduino libraries use AVR C++. For Pi, use Python libraries from PyPI (e.g., adafruit-circuitpython) which provide similar sensor drivers.
